title: Runtime of a pure-Python merge sort against the built-in sort
brief: Benchmark two ways of sorting a list of integers in CPython: the built-in sorted(), and a top-down merge sort written in pure Python inside the experiment. Use seeded pseudo-random integer lists of 1,000, 10,000 and 100,000 elements. For each size and each algorithm take the median wall-clock time of 7 repetitions (time.perf_counter), each repetition sorting a fresh copy of the same input. Check that both algorithms return the same result for every input and report that check as a metric. Report the median times at the largest size and the ratio of the two. Produce one figure: median time against input size for both algorithms, on logarithmic axes. Timings differ between executions; say so where the contract asks you to declare it.
